subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders engage effectively in collaborative discussions, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly. They come prepared (having read the material), follow agreed-upon rules, pose and respond to questions, acknowledge others' views, and, when needed, modify their own views based on new evidence.

items.prompt: Why should you come PREPARED to a discussion?

steps: Preparation means having read and thought about the material.
So you can contribute informed ideas and evidence.
So being prepared lets you discuss thoughtfully with evidence.
solution.answer: So you can contribute informed ideas supported by evidence.

items.prompt:
A classmate makes a point you hadn't considered that is backed by strong evidence.

What is a good response?

steps: Effective discussion means being open to new evidence.
So acknowledge their point and, if convinced, modify your own view.
solution.answer: Acknowledge the point and, if the evidence is strong, adjust your view.

items.prompt: What does it mean to BUILD ON others' ideas?

steps: Building on means adding to or extending what someone said.
So you connect your idea to theirs and develop the conversation.
solution.answer: Connecting your idea to theirs to extend the conversation.

items.prompt: Having read the material before a discussion is being ____.
Adding to someone's idea is ____ on it.
Changing your view with new evidence shows you are ____.
